name: DeepSeek V4 Flash DSpark — dual Spark, 1M context
statusNote: Unblocked 2026-07-30, not yet baselined. Both hard blockers are answered: greedy output is identical across boots, and the multi-node stall is gone on the clustered substrate. What remains is harness work -- arena.py can launch a venv wheel but not yet a Docker image.

blockers.what: Whether greedy token identity survives an NCCL allreduce was unmeasured, and no TP target could be ranked until it was settled.
blockers.answer: It survives. Two boots, TP2 across two Sparks, NCCL over RoCE, warmup discarded: 4/4 prompts byte-identical (see results/_multinode/determinism-2026-07-29.txt).
blockers.correction: That measurement's write-up originally credited the clean run to RDMA, implying the earlier hangs were the TCP-socket fallback. That was wrong and is retracted: the hangs recur on RoCE and are a vLLM message-queue bug (tp2-shm-broadcast-stall). The two boots here were simply two runs that did not happen to trip it -- which is also why a 4-boot baseline cannot be relied on.
blockers.sharedWith: glm-5-2-dual-spark-tp2 and every other dual-Spark recipe — this is a property of the collective, not of a model.
blockers.scope: Two boots at 8192 context, one config, four prompts. Enough to make multi-node rankable; the baseline's per-prompt stability screening still applies.

blockers.what: ulimit -l was 8 MB on both nodes, so NCCL could not use RDMA and fell back to TCP sockets. A paired ratio measured over sockets is not the recipe's hardware.
blockers.howFixed: limits.d memlock unlimited on both nodes, verified as unlimited in the launch path itself rather than in a shell.
blockers.trap: The fix READ as failed for a day. Tailscale SSH terminates inside tailscaled and never runs pam_limits, so any ulimit taken over the tailnet reports systemd's 8 MB default no matter what limits.d says. Ray workers inherit whatever launched them, so a cluster started from a tailnet session gets 8 MB memlock on every raylet and NCCL silently falls back to sockets EVEN WITH THE ROOT FIX APPLIED. Launch the head via `ssh localhost` and the worker over its LAN address, and assert unlimited on both inside the script.

blockers.what: Requests stall indefinitely at random under TP2. All three processes are READERS on vLLM's shm_broadcast queue and nobody writes: both ranks wait in worker_busy_loop for a command, the driver waits in get_response for a reply. The 100% CPU at idle GPU wattage is shm_broadcast's spin-poll.
blockers.whyItBlocks: A baseline needs 4 boots to agree. At this failure rate it will not finish, and a partial baseline is worse than none: it would define goldens from whichever prompts happened to survive.
blockers.nextStep: On the image, cheapest first: (1) --max-num-seqs 6 with VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=0, to separate the MoE kernel from the boot failure; (2) add --enforce-eager; (3) pin a shared VLLM_CACHE_ROOT across boots, which 0.26.0 needed for cross-boot identity and which is container-local here. Launcher: harness/tp2_image_launch.sh.
blockers.scope: FLEET-WIDE, not this model. Reproduced on Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 (21 GB, none of this target's kernels): warmup 1 s, request 1 fine, request 2 at ~800 prompt tokens hung the full 300 s. So this blocks every dual-Spark target, and it is tracked in benchmark.json under measurement.multiNode.fleetBlocker.
blockers.ruledOut: the interconnect (raw TCP measured 1561 MB/s during a hang), RoCE GID churn (fixed by pinning NCCL_IB_HCA; stall persists with zero warnings), NCCL itself (no rank is in a collective), async scheduling (disabled; persists), kernel JIT (zero events during a 37-minute hang), prompt shape (a 64-token prompt hung after decoding fine earlier), and memory (kv usage 0.5%).
blockers.reproduce: harness/tp2_size_bisect.sh (ascending) and its descending variant. 2-minute boots on a 21 GB model, no DeepSeek code involved.
blockers.rootCause: The arena pinned vLLM 0.26.0, which had never run multi-node on this fleet. The WORKING dual-Spark recipe (42.0/76.0 tok/s, published) runs vLLM 0.21.1rc1.dev339+g1967a5627bc3 inside aidendle94/sparkrun-vllm-ds4-gb10, with the mp headless executor. So 'we have run models on both Sparks' is true and refers to a different engine build.
blockers.notTheExecutor: Both executors fail identically -- mp and ray share multiproc_executor and shm_broadcast. Switching to mp changed nothing.
blockers.cumulativeNotSize: Ascending prompt sizes said 'fails at ~340 tokens'; descending said 'fails at ~1200' after 2230 and 1780 succeeded. Same ordinal position (3rd-4th request after boot), any size. --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 changed nothing, so not prefill chunking. Fits a ring buffer whose blocks are never reclaimed.
blockers.option1Tested: 2026-07-30. The recipe's image (vLLM 0.21.1rc1.dev339) DOES fix the stall: eight serial requests of mixed length all returned in 2-4 s, where the 0.26.0 wheel fails on request 3-4 after every boot. But the image is NOT deterministic -- one prompt, three serial requests, three different hashes -- and --max-num-seqs 1 will not boot on it at all: DeepGEMM CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS with VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=1, and 'NCCL error: unhandled cuda error' with it off. The two builds fail in opposite ways: 0.26.0 is deterministic and stalls; 0.21.1-dev is stable and is not deterministic. Neither satisfies both halves of the gate yet.
blockers.notConcurrency: The non-determinism is not batching. Requests were strictly serial, so every forward pass had batch 1 whatever the --max-num-seqs ceiling was.
blockers.howResolved: Pinned the clustered substrate. The stall is a 0.26.0 defect and does not occur on the image: 8 serial requests, 115-2225 prompt tokens, all returned in 2-4 s. Determinism came separately, from VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=0: 6/6 byte-identical over two boots sharing one VLLM_CACHE_ROOT.

blockers.what: oom-guard.sh trips at MemAvailable < 8192 MiB and killed a run that missed by 321 MiB, silently. The 6 GiB KV pin clears it, but the margin is thin and an arena arm must not die mid-measurement.
blockers.nextStep: Either raise the guard for arena runs or keep the KV pin at 6 GiB and verify headroom before each arm.

blockers.what: arena.py launches a venv wheel. It cannot launch a Docker image, so it cannot run this target even though the configuration is proven by hand.
blockers.scope: Harness code only. No unknown physics remains on this target.
blockers.nextStep: Teach Server/Cluster to launch the clustered substrate: docker run per node with the contract's dockerFlags, the target's env, NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX derived per node, and the image entrypoint. harness/tp2_image_launch.sh already does exactly this by hand and is the reference.
blockers.howResolved: arena.py grew an ImageServer: one container per node, vLLM's headless mp backend, rank 0 started first because it hosts the torch.distributed store. It derives NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX per node, mounts the repo at its own path so the patch chain needs no translation, bumps the master port every boot to dodge TIME_WAIT, and rejects any serve flag the substrate forbids. Verified: `warm` brought both nodes up and warmed all four prompt shapes.
blockers.twoTrapsFound: Writing it surfaced two omissions that the hand-written launcher had right. Without --gpus all the container starts and vLLM says 'Failed to infer device type', which names nothing useful. Without GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME, Gloo picks an interface itself and dies with 'Unable to find address for: enP7s7' -- naming a NIC that has nothing wrong with it. Both are now derived by the harness, not left to a target.

why: Worth scaffolding despite being blocked: at 1,048,576 tokens of context across two nodes with FP4 experts and FP8 dense, it exercises paths nothing else in the corpus does — and it is the recipe most likely to reward kernel work, because almost nothing on that path was written for sm_121.

served.note: First light, not a benchmark: --max-model-len 8192, NCCL over sockets because memlock is 8 MB, and there is no page-size-64 baseline to compare against because the model cannot run at 64 at all.

promptSettingsNote: d-doc-8k is ~7.7k tokens and --max-model-len is 8192, so its output budget has to be small enough to fit. A request that overruns the context aborts the arm.

cluster.hostNote: workers[].host is a LAN address reached over real OpenSSH. It must NOT be a tailnet address: tailscaled terminates the session itself and never runs pam_limits, so every raylet would inherit an 8 MB memlock and NCCL would fall back to TCP sockets without saying so.

preflight.name: sparse-mla-sm120
preflight.python: from vllm.utils.flashinfer import has_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120 as f; print(f())
preflight.hint: Almost always nvcc missing from PATH -- vLLM's has_flashinfer() is False without it because FlashInfer JITs, and the error then names the sparse MLA API, which is present and working. Check /usr/local/cuda/bin is on PATH and that the venv's bin (ninja) is still on it.

asyncSchedulingNote: MANDATORY, and it is the fix for the TP2 deadlock. Async scheduling makes max_concurrent_batches 2, which puts the engine on step_with_batch_queue -- it submits batch N+1 while collecting N. Caught mid-hang, all three processes were READERS on the shm_broadcast queue and none was in a collective: the driver waited in get_response for a reply, and both ranks waited in worker_busy_loop for a command. Nobody was writing. The 100% CPU with GPUs at idle wattage is shm_broadcast's spin-poll, which is what made this look like an NCCL problem for two days. The flag is --no-async-scheduling; note that `--async-scheduling False` silently sets it TRUE and leaves 'False' as a stray positional argument.
serveArgsNote: Proven config, 2026-07-30. --max-num-seqs is 6, NOT 1: 1 does not boot on this build, and it is not needed because the harness sends one request at a time, so every forward pass has batch 1. Do NOT add --kv-cache-memory-bytes: it skips memory profiling and the first FP8 GEMM dies with CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS. --enforce-eager is kept because cross-boot identity was measured WITH it; dropping it may be a speed win but needs its own cross-boot test. --max-model-len is 8192, not the recipe's 1M -- a 1M variant is its own target.

weights.note: 222 GB on disk. Public and ungated, so it satisfies policy.publicWeights -- but it is the largest entry cost in either arena, and it must be present on BOTH nodes.

substrateNote: This target runs on the CLUSTERED substrate (see substrate.clustered in benchmark.json): the recipe's image, vLLM 0.21.1rc1.dev339, not the 0.26.0 wheel. Its scores are not comparable with single-node targets, which is already the rule for a different wheel.
overlayNote: The flashinfer page-block-size-256 overlay is NOT needed here. It existed to make the 0.26.0 wheel serve this model at block size 256; the image already ships a build that does.
envNote: VLLM_USE_B12X_MOE=0 is MANDATORY and is the single reason this target is rankable. At 1, one prompt returns three different answers in one boot. NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX is deliberately absent -- it must be derived per node at launch (harness/gid_index.sh); it is 3 on one node and 5 on the other.
